title: Shallow Jet Spurt Engineering Model
summary: This topic seeks the development of a computationally efficient engineering-level model to predict the formation and characteristics of the "spurt" in fluid cavity created jets. The hydrodynamic spurt is the initial, often unsteady, ejection of material from the liner, preceding the formation of the main, stable jet.
description: This topic seeks the development of a computationally efficient engineering-level model to predict the formation and characteristics of the "spurt" in fluid cavity created jets. The hydrodynamic spurt is the initial, often unsteady, ejection of material from the liner, preceding the formation of the main, stable jet. Current hydrocodes can model this phenomenon but are computationally expensive and ill-suited for rapid design iteration. This project will develop a validated, reduced-order model that accurately predicts spurt velocity, mass, and geometry as a function of liner material, geometry, and threat characteristics, enabling faster design and optimization of advanced warheads.

title: Optimally Packaged Assembly for Laser Systems (OPALS)
summary: The Air Force requires light weight, compactly packaged optical systems to perform critical beam control functions for airborne high energy laser systems.
description: The Air Force requires light weight, compactly packaged optical systems to perform critical beam control functions for airborne high energy laser systems. The purpose of this topic is not to develop new outer moldlines or turret designs for airborne systems but rather focus on optimizing the packaging and performance of the internal optical system required to perform the core beam control functions. A canonical layout of such system is available in Reference 1. The Government expects the designed beam control system will perform all functions laid out in the canonical design - or that any deviations are thoroughly understood and technically justified. Additionally, designs should prioritize ease of alignment and component replacement, potential for line replaceable units, beam path conditioning, and material free of shedding contaminants which could lead to foreign object damage. In order to achieve these objectives, the Government anticipates investigations into the following areas, although this list is informational and is intended to be neither proscriptive nor comprehensive:Ruggedized Optical Design and MaterialsRobust Packaging and Assembly TechniquesNovel Optical Architectures: Explore and develop innovative optical designs inherently tolerant to vibrations, shocks, and thermal gradients.Advanced Materials Selection: Investigate and characterize advanced materials with superior thermo-mechanical properties. This includes exploring specialized glasses, ceramics, and composites for optical elements and mounting structures.Advanced Manufacturing and Assembly Processes: Investigate and implement advanced manufacturing techniques, such as additive manufacturing and precision micro-assembly, to fabricate intricate components and achieve high-precision alignment and bonding of optical elements.Athermalized Design Strategies: Implement passive and active athermalization techniques to mitigate the performance degradation caused by temperature fluctuations. This involves optimizing material choices, employing thermal compensation methods.

title: Multiple Telemetry Site Signal Source Synchronization
summary: Flight test missions that traverse multiple Test Ranges (e.g. hypersonic vehicles/weapons, cruise missiles, long-range weapon systems etc.) or that require different test support infrastructures (e.g. sea range, targets, threat simulators, etc.) at remote Test Ranges, require telemetry receive stations along the flight paths to receive real-time telemetry and then relay that data via ground…
description: Flight test missions that traverse multiple Test Ranges (e.g. hypersonic vehicles/weapons, cruise missiles, long-range weapon systems etc.) or that require different test support infrastructures (e.g. sea range, targets, threat simulators, etc.) at remote Test Ranges, require telemetry receive stations along the flight paths to receive real-time telemetry and then relay that data via ground networks to the control room monitoring the mission. In past mission pre-flight scenarios, remote telemetry receive site to control room links were checked individually. This was accomplished with a local bore sight signal simulator that transmitted a known test pattern at the center frequency of the actual test article. The telemetry receive site would receive the radio frequency signal, demodulate/decode it, then send the data via Internet protocol (IP) networks to the control room. In the control room the received data was verified to be correct as the bit pattern received could be compared to the bit pattern transmitted. This was accomplished for each local and remote telemetry receive site prior to the mission.During the test, each local and remote telemetry receive site would send data to the control room and a manual switch would be accomplished between each data source based on data quality that was determined manually. Note, this selection was not automated.With the invent of best source selection using data quality metrics transferred over IP networks via data quality encapsulation [1], no longer is election of multiple data sources done manually. Telemetry receivers now assess received data quality and assign a bit error probability to a packet of data prior to sending it to the best source selector in the control room. A best source selector (BSS) inputs these multiple streams, performs time alignment, then using the data quality metric, selects the best data to output on a bit-by-bit basis. This output is the best data using all available data streams from diverse receive sites.Though higher quality, near error-free data is now provided to the control room, the addition of the BSS has revealed a shortfall. The entire data path from remote receive sites to transport through best source selection to control room cannot be tested as a complete system to assess mission readiness. The traditional method of pre-flight checks cannot be used. Why? The best source selector will not be able to correlate the multiple data streams from remote sites as the signal sources will not be correlated. This results in the configuration and operation of the BSS being unknown until the test mission. The proposed work will focus on solving this shortfall resulting in a networked, synchronized telemetry validation system capable of simulating a test vehicle's telemetry signal at multiple ground stations simultaneously. Stated another way, the proposed system must simulate the test article signal as if all telemetry receive stations could “see” the test article and simultaneously receive the telemetry signal. This capability will allow test ranges to perform pre-mission verification of the entire telemetry infrastructure. This would include all participating receive antennas, distribution networks, and best source selector(s) to control room displays to ensure full system connectivity and performance before supporting a live mission.

title: Long Rod Delivery System
summary: The lack of a non-destructive, high-precision launching method for high length-to-diameter (L/D) projectiles fundamentally degrades the fidelity of Live Fire Test and Evaluation (LFT&E) data.
description: The lack of a non-destructive, high-precision launching method for high length-to-diameter (L/D) projectiles fundamentally degrades the fidelity of Live Fire Test and Evaluation (LFT&E) data. For the Air Force, this deficiency directly compromises the development of penetrating munitions, degrades the survivability assessments of aerospace platforms, and introduces significant acquisition risks due to flawed test data and increased testing costs. Currently, there is not means of reliably controlling or manipulating the flight of a long rod projectile such that it consistently reaches a target location at a specific orientation. Providing means of accomplishing this feat advances DoW test capabilities for critical data underpinning analytical vulnerability assessments and engineering designs improving the survivability posture of current and next generation combat aircraft.

title: Luminescence-Based Surface Measurement Technique for Simultaneous Pressure and Temperature Measurements within Non-Oxygen Based Hypersonic Ground Test Facilities
summary: Within aerodynamic testing, pressure sensitive paint (PSP) provides crucial global surface pressure data that is utilized in calculating aerodynamic loads [1] and identifying small scale features within the flow. The working principle behind PSP involves luminophores that fluoresce at an intensity inversely proportional to the number of oxygen molecules present i.e., oxygen quenching [2].
description:
Within aerodynamic testing, pressure sensitive paint (PSP) provides crucial global surface pressure data that is utilized in calculating aerodynamic loads [1] and identifying small scale features within the flow. The working principle behind PSP involves luminophores that fluoresce at an intensity inversely proportional to the number of oxygen molecules present i.e., oxygen quenching [2].
While these paints/luminophores have been sufficiently researched, the use-case of these paints is severely limited due to the requirement of oxygen in the flow field. Advanced hypersonic wind tunnels such as the blowdown facility at AEDC Tunnel No. 9 which utilizes nitrogen as the working fluid, are unable to utilize PSP to capture global pressure data with this method and are therefore severely limited to discrete measurement techniques. It is required that a novel technique be developed to capture simultaneous global pressure and temperature measurements in nonoxygen-based hypersonic wind tunnels.

title: High Speed, Low Temperature Hyperspectral Imager for High Enthalpy Ground Testing
summary: AEDC requires a method to resolve temperature and emissivity across the surface of test articles. Specifically, there is a need for a high-speed low-temperature measurement solution that overlaps with other higher-temperature capabilities.
description: AEDC requires a method to resolve temperature and emissivity across the surface of test articles. Specifically, there is a need for a high-speed low-temperature measurement solution that overlaps with other higher-temperature capabilities. The solution threshold requirements are to measure surface temperature from 0-1500 F (2000 F objective), at 4000 Hz (5000 Hz objective), with a pixel footprint of at most 0.1 inch (0.05 inch objective) and an accuracy of +/- 10 deg F (+/- 5 deg F objective).

title: Reusable Illumination System
summary: The PF300 flash bulbs, that provide high-intensity illumination for high-speed video acquisition, are no longer in production. The objective is to award a contract to a small business to engineer, design, and manufacture a modern, robust, reusable replacement for the legacy PF300 flash bulb.
description: The PF300 flash bulbs, that provide high-intensity illumination for high-speed video acquisition, are no longer in production. The objective is to award a contract to a small business to engineer, design, and manufacture a modern, robust, reusable replacement for the legacy PF300 flash bulb. This new system must meet or surpass the existing illumination and performance requirements of the original flash bulbs to ensure seamless integration with current high-speed video systems. The ideal solution would leverage Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or near-COTS technologies to qualify this project as a direct-to-Phase-II effort. A successful reusable replacement would immediately solve the impending obsolescence issue, securing a reliable illumination source for future missions. Furthermore, transitioning to a reusable system would dramatically reduce consumable cost. This technological update could also pave the way for enhanced capabilities, such as adjustable light intensity and longer duration illumination, offering greater flexibility and improved data quality for high-speed video analysis across various applications

title: Technical Data Package Modernization for Information Assurance and Secure Data Exchange
summary: Background and Problem Statement: The modernization of Technical Data Packages (TDPs) is imperative to address the Air and Space Force’s operational challenges in securely managing large-scale, complex datasets associated with advanced platforms and their sustainment life cycles.
description:
Background and Problem Statement:
The modernization of Technical Data Packages (TDPs) is imperative to address the Air and Space Force’s operational challenges in securely managing large-scale, complex datasets associated with advanced platforms and their sustainment life cycles. Current TDP systems often lack robust Information Assurance (IA) capabilities, seamless integration with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) environments, and effective mechanisms for secure data exchange across operational networks. This limitation not only hinders data integrity and configuration control but also increases vulnerabilities to cyber threats, jeopardizing mission-critical operations. The rapid pace of platform evolution and the increasing reliance on Model-Based Definition (MBD) and digital twin technologies further exacerbate the need for a comprehensive solution that ensures TDP security, scalability, and operational readiness.

Opportunity and Desired Outcome:
This Directed to Phase II (D2P2) SBIR effort aims to develop an innovative, scalable, and secure solution to modernize TDPs to support the lifecycle of highly complex Air and Space Force platforms. The envisioned solution will integrate advanced IA protocols, cryptographic protections, and tools for encrypted data exchange to facilitate the secure management of the "as-sustained" configuration state of critical assets. The outcome will be a functional prototype capable of enabling secure TDP lifecycle management while aligning with the Trusted AI and Autonomy modernization priorities and Zero Trust Architecture principles. The proposed solution will enhance operational efficiency, minimize cyber risks, and establish a foundation for scalable implementation across DoD platforms.

The project’s Technology Readiness Level (TRL) at the start is anticipated to be TRL 4, with the target of reaching a minimum TRL 6 by the conclusion of Phase II, including validation of core capabilities in a relevant operational environment.

Required Efforts and Phase Activities:
To achieve the stated objectives, the following efforts and activities are required for each phase of the project:

Phase II:

Develop a secure visualization tool for displaying large-scale MBD geometry and associated data through encrypted web-based interfaces.
Implement an encrypted configuration management system to maintain and update the "as-sustained" asset state while ensuring strict data integrity.
Create advanced tools for automated data quality checks, incorporating rules-based IA compliance validation to ensure all TDPs meet security and contractual requirements.
Design an end-to-end encrypted exchange framework for TDPs, incorporating user authentication, authorization, and audit trails while conforming to DoD Zero Trust Architecture guidelines.
Integrate AI/ML methodologies to enable secure damage detection, sustainment planning, and actionable insights into asset health.
Demonstrate the prototype in an operationally relevant environment, proving feasibility, security compliance, and system performance in handling large and diverse data streams.

Minimum Deliverables:

A secure web-based MBD visualization prototype capable of rendering large-scale geometry and TDP datasets with sub-second response times and role-based access controls.
Tools for encrypted configuration management and secure "as-sustained" state maintenance, integrated with PLM systems.
An automated framework for data quality checks and IA compliance validation of TDPs using defined security protocols and rules-based engines.
A cryptographic data transfer and exchange framework, with test results demonstrating alignment with DoD security policies and successful inter-organizational data exchange.
Technical documentation detailing methodologies, system architecture, and IA protocols implemented during the project, including recommendations for further scaling and operationalization.
A transition plan for integrating the developed TDP modernization technology into operational environments within the Air and Space Force platforms, supported by a detailed commercialization strategy aligned with mission needs.

Significance and Contribution to DoD Objectives:
The proposed solution directly addresses the Operational Imperative 7—Readiness to Deploy and Fight—by delivering secure and reliable tools for managing critical asset data. The project also supports the DoD’s Trusted AI and Autonomy priorities by incorporating advanced data protection mechanisms, secure autonomous processes, and scalable solutions for data management across platforms. Successful execution of this effort will enhance the DoD’s ability to maintain readiness, ensure data security, and streamline collaboration with stakeholders while safeguarding sensitive information in a rapidly evolving threat landscape.

title: US Production of Ultra-High Temperature Ceramic-Yielding Preceramic Polymers
summary: The scaled production of C/C-UHTCs composites (UHTCMCs) for defense applications requires the manufacturing of UHTC precursors in quantities sufficient to support acquisition programs. This SBIR will establish production of an AFRL-patented UHTC preceramic polymers so that the materials are available, at scale and affordable price point, to the high-temperature composite production community.
description: The scaled production of C/C-UHTCs composites (UHTCMCs) for defense applications requires the manufacturing of UHTC precursors in quantities sufficient to support acquisition programs. This SBIR will establish production of an AFRL-patented UHTC preceramic polymers so that the materials are available, at scale and affordable price point, to the high-temperature composite production community.

title: Low SWaP, 2-micron Fiber Amplifiers
summary: High-power fiber lasers operating in the 2-micron regime offer critical advantages for defense, medical, and industrial applications, including eye-safer directed energy, advanced sensing, and precision materials processing.
description: High-power fiber lasers operating in the 2-micron regime offer critical advantages for defense, medical, and industrial applications, including eye-safer directed energy, advanced sensing, and precision materials processing. While kilowatt-class, narrow-linewidth thulium-doped fiber amplifiers have been demonstrated, the Department of the Air Force aims to reduce the size and weight of existing kilowatt-class 2-micron fiber amplifiers into a highly compact system with similar size, weight, and power metrics of existing 1-micron fiber amplifiers. This topic seeks to leverage existing Air Force laboratory architectures to prime industry for production of robust 2-micron fiber amplifiers, paving the way for transition into active directed energy programs.

title: Agile Wire Harness Manipulation and Installation for Unmanned Aerial Systems
summary: Context & BackgroundModern Department of Defense (DoD) manufacturing and depot sustainment environments increasingly depend on agile automation to scale up production and maintain rapid operational readiness. While automated assembly technologies have matured substantially for rigid components with predictable geometries, the handling of flexible materials remains a persistent challenge.
description: Context & BackgroundModern Department of Defense (DoD) manufacturing and depot sustainment environments increasingly depend on agile automation to scale up production and maintain rapid operational readiness. While automated assembly technologies have matured substantially for rigid components with predictable geometries, the handling of flexible materials remains a persistent challenge. Specifically, wire harness routing, connector inspection, and insertion operations are ubiquitous across the production lines of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS), advanced munitions families, and autonomous collaborative platforms. Currently, these intricate electrical assembly processes represent a bottleneck in UAS assembly operations. Assembly technicians must manually route non-rigid cables through confined structural cavities and execute high-precision connection steps under high-mix, low-volume production conditions. Traditional industrial robotics break down when tasked with these operations because flexible wiring deforms unpredictably during manipulation, completely violating the rigid-part assumptions and fixed, hard-tooled rules of standard automation. Problem, Opportunity, & Unmet Need The complete reliance on manual wire harness installation creates a critical capability deficiency that severely penalizes DoD manufacturing agility and surge capacity. Manual operations are fundamentally non-scalable, meaning production lines cannot dynamically "ramp-to-rate" to meet sudden spikes in theater demand. Furthermore, manual wire routing and insertion introduce human-induced variability, resulting in unquantifiable defects such as partially seated connectors, overstressed wires, or compromised bend radii. These latent defects frequently slip past standard visual inspections and surface as catastrophic electrical or communication failures during critical mission times. Aerospace prime contractors and program offices have identified this manual chokepoint as the largest automation gap in UAS and munitions production. This deficiency creates a major opportunity to implement a flexible automation solution. Resolving this challenge requires a modular, adaptive robotic workcell that handles deformable materials, operates with high positional accuracy in restricted footprints, and can be rapidly retasked between completely different product designs within a single factory shift. Desired Outcome & Technological Improvement The desired outcome of this research and development effort is a fully integrated, single-arm modular robotic manufacturing workcell capable of autonomously handling the core manipulation and installation scenarios for flexible UAS and munitions wiring harnesses. Shifting the technology from manual assembly to adaptive, sensor-driven automation will fundamentally advance the DoD technological state of the art by achieving the following targeted improvements: Deformable Material Control: The platform will combine deterministic offline path planning with adaptive, real-time online sensory feedback (such as tactile, force-torque, and vision monitoring). This closed-loop configuration enables "search and settle" machine behaviors to dynamically correct for micro-misalignments and part variability on the fly. Sub-Millimeter Tolerances: The workcell will successfully execute precise connector insertion and blind-mate assembly steps within tightly constrained geometries to a targeted positioning tolerance of $\le$ 0.5 mm.Rapid Retaskability: The system will break the paradigm of dedicated single-product manufacturing by allowing shop-floor operators to ingest new geometric data and completely retask the workcell to a novel harness family in less than 8 hours.End-to-End Digital Thread: The workcell will generate machine-readable traceability records of every insertion force profile and routing path. This delivers a reliable data audit trail to eliminate quality escapes and predict latent field defects before they manifest in flight.Minimum Acceptable DeliverablesThe following deliverables must be successfully turned over to the government to satisfy the performance requirements of this solicitation:Integrated Single-Arm Robotic Workcell: One fully functional, operational modular automation cell comprising a COTS collaborative arm manipulator, reconfigurable mounting base, interchangeable end-effectors, integrated real-time compute block, and the complete multi-modal sensor stack (vision, tactile, and force-torque instrumentation). Autonomous Software Stack & Executables: Full, unencumbered delivery of the native software architecture, including the offline CAD data-ingestion pipeline, real-time adaptive control algorithms, and localized vision-tactile tracking scripts, along with complete integration documentation.Cross-Program Retasking Report: A documented technical package demonstrating the step-by-step procedures, software tools, and data workflows used to successfully transition the physical workcell between two distinct harness families in less than 8 hours.Comprehensive Technical Data Package (TDP): System layout schematics, wiring diagrams, universal end-effector interface control documents, operational manuals, and interface guides for MES/ERP factory network synchronization. Final Performance & Verification Report: A verified engineering data package from the live prime facility demonstration detailing empirical success metrics. This must validate insertion position accuracy ($\le$ 0.5 mm), insertion force variance curves, production cycle time gains ($\ge$ 2x throughput), labor hour compression ($\ge$ 50%), and a sample data pull of the machine-readable digital thread registry.

title: Agile Autonomous Technical Data Package to Path Robotic Task Specification
summary: Here is a draft for a Direct to Phase II SBIR solicitation topic based on the technical capabilities of the data extraction and automated path-planning pipeline.
description: Here is a draft for a Direct to Phase II SBIR solicitation topic based on the technical capabilities of the data extraction and automated path-planning pipeline. The content has been carefully structured to be precise and concise while protecting all proprietary text.Direct to Phase II Topic DraftTopic ObjectiveObjective: Develop and demonstrate an automated, end-to-end software platform capable of ingesting heterogeneous Technical Data Packages (TDPs)—including 3D CAD models, 2D engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), and textual specifications—to autonomously extract engineering intent and generate optimized, collision-free robotic inspection trajectories without manual waypoint programming or hard-coded scripting.The resulting system must bridge the gap between enterprise digital design data and physical automation by converting complex tolerances, geometric constraints, and manufacturing annotations into a standardized data model, simulating the execution in a physics-accurate virtual sandbox, and deploying executable inspection commands directly to physical mobile robotic manipulators. The objective is to drastically compress quality control programming timelines from days to under two hours and enable rapid robotic reconfiguration in highly agile manufacturing environments.Topic DescriptionBackground & Problem Statement: Modern aerospace manufacturing and sustainment pipelines face severe bottlenecks due to legacy quality control (QC) practices. As defense systems shift toward highly modular, rapidly evolving, and low-cost attritable architectures, traditional fixed automation becomes commercially and operationally impractical. Traditional robotic inspection lines require highly specialized programmers to manually teach waypoints, configure physical sensor triggers, and execute tedious trial-and-error collision testing on vendor-specific offline programming utilities. This labor-intensive paradigm introduces severe production delays, as errors or dimensional variations are often caught late in the assembly stream, resulting in compounding downstream costs and extended lead times.While digital enterprise structures routinely house complete engineering intent within comprehensive Technical Data Packages (TDPs)—complete with 3D geometry, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) markers, material specifications, and assembly metadata—translating this multi-format data into actionable instructions remains a manual and error-prone process. To meet the demand for rapid production scaling and point-of-need deployment, the Department of the Air Force requires an intelligent software layer that dynamically parses TDP data and translates it directly into autonomous robotic execution paths.Phase II Expected Outcomes: Proposers responding to this Direct to Phase II topic must demonstrate a mature conceptual foundation, such as completed preliminary software blocks or data-parsing prototypes originally validated under related early-stage research. Phase II efforts must deliver a hardened, end-to-end software prototype validated against representative aerospace assembly geometries.Key technical deliverables include the ingestion/planning software, documentation for enterprise data interfaces, and localized simulation proof-of-concepts. The system performance will be benchmarked against key parameters, targeting a setup time reduction to under 8 hours for novel manufacturing configurations and compressing numerical programming timelines down to less than 1.5 hours. Final validation should culminate in a software-driven execution demo using either high-fidelity simulations or physical manufacturing hardware within a pilot production framework.

title: Advanced Reserve Power Source Technologies
summary: Power source performance in terms of power and energy density is the major objective with affordability, safety, and reliability secondary objectives of Air Force Armament Directorate programs for advanced reserve power sources for weapon systems.
description: Power source performance in terms of power and energy density is the major objective with affordability, safety, and reliability secondary objectives of Air Force Armament Directorate programs for advanced reserve power sources for weapon systems. Secondary objectives are not distant relative to the major objective, but power and energy density is emphasized in order to enable new concepts and integration strategies. Current reserve thermally activated battery technology is at risk of becoming obsolete due to increasing specific power and specific energy requirements, while other battery technologies with similar or greater specific energy suffer from multiple failure modes, have limited storage life, or have not been tailored to meet the unique requirements for Air Force weapon programs. An advanced reserve power source lasting 20+ years without the need for maintenance or significant energy loss while in storage, is reliable, and is inherently safe, e.g. is not susceptible to thermal runaway, is required. Weapons typically have storage lifetimes of 20+ years; and must maintain reliable operation at any point within this time period without the power source being inadvertently activated. When the power source is activated, it must rise to full voltage within 600 ms and have an activated life of 5+ minutes. The power source must be able to survive shock, vibration, and temperatures (MIL-HDBK-310 1% Hot/ 1% Cold Days, worldwide) associated with external and internal carriage, high speed free flight, and storage environments. The power source will be required to provide power for weapon avionics, guidance, and ordnance initiation events for the entire flight profile. The load on the power source must be capable of periods of pulse power with an average 2.5 kW/kg minimum and a goal to exceed 5 kW/kg load over 60 seconds. The goal of this technology development is to design, develop, and test an advanced design for a power source capable of 20+ years of storage, 5+ minutes of activated life, with a specific energy at a minimum of 40 Wh/kg and a goal to exceed 100 Wh/kg. The power source must be inherently safe during its entire lifetime. Due to the safety issues associated with lithium battery technologies and the process to receive certification through the Naval Ordnance Security and Safety Activity (NOSSA) for use on an ordnance system, lithium battery technologies will need to demonstrate no venting under NAVSEA S9310-AQ-SAF-010 test conditions.

title: G-TEAD USAREUR-AF ACE 27-02: Spectrum Enabled Warfare Powered by xTech
summary: The operational challenge on the Eastern Flank is the enablement of U.S. Army forces, operating within a North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and joint coalition framework, to sense, understand, exploit, attack, and protect across a contested electromagnetic environment and connected cyberspace.
description:
The operational challenge on the Eastern Flank is the enablement of U.S. Army forces, operating within a North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and joint coalition framework, to sense, understand, exploit, attack, and protect across a contested electromagnetic environment and connected cyberspace. To deter peer aggression and preserve freedom of maneuver, V Corps must protect tactical command and control networks while delivering synchronized, non-lethal and lethal effects at depth against adversary command, control, communications, and targeting architectures.

Gaining and maintaining spectrum superiority against dense anti-access / area denial systems requires a modular, coalition-interoperable architecture that operates in congested radio frequency (RF) environments, executes multi-echelon precision effects, and hardens friendly formations against persistent electromagnetic and cyber disruption during competition, crisis, and conflict. The Army requires capabilities that are scalable, upgradeable, intuitive for Soldiers across military occupational specialties, and maintainable at the tactical edge without routine reliance on field service representatives for minor repairs or adjustments.

The Army is seeking to evaluate capabilities to participate in one of three demonstration tracks (eligible for SBIR follow-on contacts) as part of this Spectrum Enabled Warfare ACE:

Capability 1: Electromagnetic Support / Tactical Surveillance

Capability 2: Autonomous Network Management

Capability 3: Electromagnetic Environment Visualization and Battle Damage Assessment Tools

Full competition details including details on the topic areas of interest can be found in Appendix A section of the G-TEAD USAREUR-AF ACE 27-02: Spectrum Enabled Warfare Powered by xTech RFI here: https://www.xtech.army.mil/competitions/.

title: ONR Open Topic for Low-Cost Heads Up Displays (HUDs) for Virtual & Augmented Reality (VR/AR)

description:

title: AI-Enabled Computed Vision Air-to-Air Refueling Performance Assessment and Automated Pilot Debrief System
summary: Air-to-air refueling (AAR) is a critical Department of the Air Force and Department of the Navy capability enabling global mobility, long-range strike, combat airpower projection, and sustained aviation operations. However, aerial refueling remains one of the most technically demanding and safety-critical aviation tasks performed by aircrews.
description: Air-to-air refueling (AAR) is a critical Department of the Air Force and Department of the Navy capability enabling global mobility, long-range strike, combat airpower projection, and sustained aviation operations. However, aerial refueling remains one of the most technically demanding and safety-critical aviation tasks performed by aircrews. Successful execution requires precise aircraft positioning, coordinated control inputs, accurate closure rate management, continuous situational awareness, and effective crew coordination between tanker and receiver aircraft.Current aerial refueling training and post-flight assessment processes rely heavily on instructor observation, pilot self-assessment, manual video review, and subjective evaluation of performance. These approaches provide limited ability to quantitatively assess the thousands of individual performance variables that influence successful refueling operations. Existing methods do not provide pilots with objective, moment-by-moment feedback on aircraft positioning, closure rates, control inputs, deviations from desired procedures, or trends in individual performance over time.This topic seeks to develop, demonstrate, and transition an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled computed vision capability that (post-flight) automatically analyzes aerial refueling operations and provides objective, data-driven pilot performance feedback. The desired capability will mature existing advances in autonomous aerial refueling analytics and apply them toward training, readiness, and safety improvement by transforming aerial refueling video and available aircraft performance data into actionable post-flight debrief products.The developed system shall provide an automated “hot wash” which analyzes aerial refueling events, identifies performance deviations, and generates intuitive visualizations that allow pilots and instructors to better understand execution quality and areas for improvement. The system shall reduce reliance on subjective recollection and manual review by providing objective measurements of aircraft performance throughout the refueling profile.The capability shall focus on analysis of tanker-mounted video data, such as KC-46 aerial refueling camera systems, while maintaining an architecture capable of expanding across additional tanker and receiver platforms. The vendor may pick (with Government concurrence) the first 3-5 receiver platforms to use in developing this system. Future applicability includes KC-135, C-17, all fighter receiver aircraft, naval aviation communities, autonomous aerial refueling systems, and other aviation training environments requiring advanced performance analytics.The desired solution shall leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and advanced human-machine interfaces to provide capabilities including:• Automated detection and tracking of tanker (boom and hose) and receiver aircraft during aerial refueling operations.• Measurement of relative aircraft position, movement, velocity, and alignment throughout the refueling engagement.• Assessment of aircraft position within the approved refueling envelope.• Analysis of closure rates, approach vectors, aircraft stability, and deviations from nominal procedures.• Ability to correlate video with other aircraft data if/as available (e.g. telemetry, fuel transfer rate, fuel state, and pilot inputs) to evaluate performance drivers.• Generation of objective performance scores and trend analysis across multiple training events.• Creation of visual performance assessment products for receiver pilot post-flight review of their performance during refueling, including graphical overlays, heat maps, event timelines, and immersive or interactive debrief environments.• Support for instructor review, adjudication, and refinement of automated assessments during initial deployment.The system should evaluate innovative approaches for integrating automated analytics with existing or future aviation training environments, including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), mission rehearsal systems, simulator environments, or other computer-based training tools.The solution must address operational challenges associated with military aviation data, including secure processing of controlled aviation video, automated data protection, and protection of sensitive operational information. The capability should consider approaches for minimizing processing burden on operational units while enabling rapid generation of post-flight assessments.The Government seeks solutions which provide an operationally relevant prototype supporting aerial refueling training organizations. Successful completion of this effort will provide Air Force and joint aviation communities with a next-generation training and assessment capability that improves pilot proficiency, increases the training value of each refueling event, reduces equipment damage and maintenance impacts, and enhances overall mission readiness.The desired end state is an operationally demonstrated capability ready to implement for at least one type of receiver aircraft and that can support transition into existing aviation training ecosystems and provide a scalable foundation for future AI-enabled aviation performance assessment across the Department of Defense.

title: Cyber Resiliency for Fog and Edge Computing Devices
summary: This topic is intended for technology proven ready to move directly into a Phase II. Therefore, a Phase I award is not required. The offeror is required to provide detailed documentation in the Direct to Phase II proposal which demonstrates accomplishment of a "Phase I-like" effort, including a feasibility study.
description: This topic is intended for technology proven ready to move directly into a Phase II. Therefore, a Phase I award is not required. The offeror is required to provide detailed documentation in the Direct to Phase II proposal which demonstrates accomplishment of a "Phase I-like" effort, including a feasibility study. This feasibility study should include an approach, architecture and previous demonstration of a limited-scope prototype with the ability to prevent or mitigate a single class of cyber-attacks on an edge-node device, embedded device, or a similar device. The approach should be capable of scaling to a large of number of edge-nodes and have the ability to autonomously detect and respond to an attack.

title: Fusion of Cooperative Information Sharing for Uncrewed Air Systems (FOCISAUS)
summary: Distributed air operations increasingly depend on timely awareness of objects, hazards, and activities beyond the field of view of any individual platform. Cooperative perception offers a path to extend sensing coverage and reduce blind spots by allowing multiple platforms and supporting nodes to share sensor-derived information.
description:
Distributed air operations increasingly depend on timely awareness of objects, hazards, and activities beyond the field of view of any individual platform. Cooperative perception offers a path to extend sensing coverage and reduce blind spots by allowing multiple platforms and supporting nodes to share sensor-derived information. Yet this benefit is limited by the large size of modern sensor data, the variability of wireless links, the need for rapid decision making, and the difficulty of combining observations from different platforms, geometries, and sensing modalities.
This topic seeks prototype-ready solutions that build on prior feasibility work in distributed information sharing, compression, adaptive transmission, and sensor data fusion. The government is interested in capabilities that can select and transmit the most relevant information, manage latency and bandwidth constraints, and fuse data from multiple sources into improved perception outputs for autonomy or operator use.
Offerors should address the data fusion aspect as a core requirement of the overall solution, whether through point cloud fusion, image or radar correlation, feature or object fusion, track association, or other mission-appropriate methods. Solutions should also describe how fused outputs are exposed to mission applications, edge processing nodes, or user interfaces. Approaches that can operate under degraded or intermittent communications and can scale across multiple sensing platforms are of particular interest.
Prototype capabilities may include, but are not limited to: Distributed organization, naming, publication, discovery, or retrieval of sensor information; Adaptive data selection, fidelity control, compression, and transmission policies; Real-time or near-real-time fusion and correlation of data from multiple platforms or sensor types; Delivery of fused perception products to autonomy software, edge analytics, or mobile mission applications; and Measurable improvements in latency, bandwidth efficiency, blind-spot reduction, and detection or tracking performance.
